# Dad-Friendly Keys Gap → Harpers Ferry Finish Hike

## The Two Options

### Option 1: Easier/Moderate (the one I'd pick)
**Keys Gap (VA-WV 9) → Harpers Ferry / ATC HQ** — **~6.3 miles, NOBO**

A downhill-trending, half-day finish. You drop about 600 feet over the route. The trail rolls gently through hardwood forest, crosses under the Route 340 bridge, and then descends into Harpers Ferry with the railroad bridge and river views as your finish-line welcome. ATC HQ is right in lower town.

This is the right call if Dad wants a relaxed Tuesday: sleep in, start mid-morning, walk at conversation pace, finish by early afternoon, and celebrate in town.

### Option 2: Longer (if Dad is feeling good)
**Weverton → Harpers Ferry / ATC HQ** — **~16.2 miles, SOBO-style**

Start at Weverton, climb Weverton Cliffs for Potomac views, then continue southbound along the ridge and down through the same Keys Gap → Harpers Ferry corridor. Twice the mileage, a real climb early, but a big-day finish with river-and-cliffs payoff. Only do this if Dad has been doing 14+ mile days comfortably and wants the longer story.

---

## Parking & Shuttle

This is the part that needs tightening before you go. The basic shape:

**Plan A — two vehicles:** Leave one car in Harpers Ferry at the NPS visitor lot (check if the ATC lot or lower-town parking works better on a Tuesday). Drive the second car to Keys Gap (or Weverton) together. Hike. Retrieve the Keys Gap car afterward. Easiest, no shuttle dependency.

**Plan B — one vehicle + shuttle:** Park at Harpers Ferry. Arrange a morning shuttle to Keys Gap (or Weverton). Local shuttle drivers service this corridor — confirm availability for a Tuesday, since midweek is quieter. ATC HQ can often provide a list of current shuttle drivers, or check the ATC Trail Updates page / FarOut comments.

**What I don't have yet:** exact shuttle driver names, current phone numbers, and whether Keys Gap parking is legal and unobstructed on a weekday. Keys Gap is a busy VA-WV 9 crossing; parking space exists but verify it's not signed no-parking and not a tow-away zone. *Verify all three before locking the date.*

---

## Water

The 6.3-mile Keys Gap route is a short day-hike by AT standards. One or two liters per person is usually enough for a spring or early-summer morning. There are no reliable on-trail water sources between Keys Gap and Harpers Ferry — this is a dry ridge walk. **Carry all water from the start.**

For the longer Weverton option, plan to carry 2–3 liters and confirm whether a seasonal stream or spigot is running at the Weverton parking area or at Gathland/Ed Garvey (not on-route for the SOBO direction, but relevant for bailout). Check FarOut or current Maryland DNR water reports before extending the day.

---

## Weather

The NWS point I pulled was for Dad's last Garmin fix (Chester Gap, ~50 miles south), so this is directional only. For Keys Gap / Harpers Ferry, pull a fresh NWS point-forecast at 39.3223, -77.7381 or search "Harpers Ferry, WV." That said: the regional picture in the forecast shows no active alerts, mild temps (40s–70s), and only a slight chance of rain Saturday. For a Tuesday hike, check the 48-hour forecast the Sunday before. 

**The main weather risk on this corridor:** heat. If the Tuesday high is pushing 85°F+, start early (7–8 AM), carry extra water, and watch Dad for slowdown or dizziness. There's almost no exposed ridgeline on the Keys Gap route — it's mostly tree-covered — so sun exposure is manageable.

**VA stomach bug alert (11 hours ago):** A stomach bug is circulating on the AT in Virginia. Dad should be extra careful about hand hygiene before eating, filtering/treating water even at developed spigots, and not sharing food or bottles with other hikers. Carry hand sanitizer and use it.

---

## Bailout

The beauty of the 6.3-mile Keys Gap route is that there *isn't* a deep bailout problem. If something goes wrong, you're at most an hour or two from either end.

- **Nearly at start:** walk back to the car at Keys Gap.
- **Mid-route (mile 2-4):** you're in the woods between VA-WV 9 and the Route 340 underpass. There is no intermediate road crossing. The move here is to assess whether Dad can continue slowly or if someone needs to hike out the way they came.
- **Near the finish (Route 340 underpass, mile ~5):** you're practically in town. Continue downhill to ATC HQ or have the pickup meet you at the pedestrian bridge.

For the 16-mile Weverton option, the bailout adds complexity: Keys Gap (VA-WV 9) at roughly the halfway point is the natural exit if Dad is fading. Confirm a shuttle driver willing to do a mid-hike pickup before attempting the longer route.

---

## 1-Day NOBO from Pine Grove Furnace State Park

Pine Grove Furnace is a great launch point — the AT runs right through the park, you're at the traditional halfway marker, and you have a camp store, water, and bathrooms at the start. For a single day northbound, you have one main decision: **out-and-back or car-spot / shuttle.**

### Mileage Options (Route-Order Guardrails)

All distances are approximate; confirm with your guide or FarOut before leaving.

| Option | Route | One-Way Miles | Round-Trip / Total |
|--------|-------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Short day** | Pine Grove → AT halfway area / Pole Steeple loop or out toward James Fry, turn around | 3–5 mi | 6–10 mi |
| **Moderate day** | Pine Grove → James Fry Shelter side trail, turn around | ~7.2 mi | ~14.4 mi |
| **Strong day (point-to-point)** | Pine Grove → Alec Kennedy Shelter | ~15.3 mi | Needs shuttle |

For a first-timer or anyone testing gear, the **moderate out-and-back toward James Fry** is the sweet spot: you get a real trail day, you touch the AT, and your car is waiting at the finish.

### Parking

Pine Grove Furnace State Park has a large lot near the camp store / AT museum area. Parking is generally available on weekdays. On spring/summer weekends, arrive early — the Ironmaster's Mansion hostel and day-use crowd fill it. If the main lot is full, there's overflow near Fuller Lake. No overnight permit needed for day parking, but check the park's current rules.

**Shuttle:** If you do a point-to-point to Alec Kennedy (~15.3 mi), you'll need a pickup at the PA 233 or PA 34 road crossings. No guaranteed shuttle service at that endpoint — you'll need to park a second car or arrange a driver. No ride-share reliability to count on in that area.

### Water

- **At the start:** Spigot/seasonal water at the park (camp store, Ironmaster's area). Confirm flow before you rely on it.
- **En route to James Fry:** The shelter side trail (~7.2 mi in) has a water source, but it's seasonal and can be unreliable in dry May stretches. Carry what you need — don't plan on filtering there unless you've seen a recent FarOut comment confirming flow.
- **Between James Fry and Alec Kennedy:** Water sources exist but are even less dependable. If you go that far, check recent comments.

**Rule of thumb:** Carry 2–3 liters from Pine Grove. If you find water on trail, great — but don't need it.

### Weather (May 2026)

No current NWS forecast for Pine Grove coordinates in this fetch. Before you leave, check the NWS point forecast for Pine Grove Furnace (roughly 40.03, -77.30).

May in this stretch: mild to warm (50s–70s°F), but rain is common. Afternoon thunderstorms are possible. The trail here is mostly ridge-and-valley walking — no exposed ridge lines like the Whites, so lightning exposure is moderate, not extreme. Still: if a thunderstorm is in the forecast, shorten the day and turn around early.

If rain is forecast all day, still go — just keep the miles modest, pack dry sleep clothes (even on a day hike), and accept you're getting wet.

### Bailout

- **Early bailout:** Just turn around. The trail back to Pine Grove is always the safest exit.
- **Midday bailout:** If you've passed the halfway point toward James Fry and something goes wrong, the nearest road crossing is at PA 233 a few miles south of the shelter. Not a casual roadside pickup spot, but it's a paved road.
- **If you feel off:** Sore feet are normal. Cold, confused, cramping, or vomiting are not — those are stop signals.

### Final Checklist

- [ ] **Guide loaded:** Confirm mileages in FarOut or your guidebook — the route-order validator says James Fry is ~7.2 mi, but confirm the exact number and shelter side-trail distance.
- [ ] **Water:** Carry 2–3 liters from the start. Check one recent FarOut comment on James Fry water.
- [ ] **Weather:** Pull the NWS point forecast morning-of. Cancel or shorten for thunderstorms.

### The Water Problem (the real one)

Your route validator already flags this: Shenandoah shelters/huts have water sources, but **late-summer reliability is not guaranteed**. The springs and streams at Calf Mountain, Blackrock, Pinefield, and Hightop can slow to a trickle or dry up in a hot, dry July. With only 2L capacity:

- On Day 1 you'd need Calf Mountain's water to be running at mile 8.6 to reach Blackrock at mile 21.6.
- On Day 2 you'd need Blackrock and/or a mid-day source to reach Pinefield.

1. **Confirm water before you go.** Recent FarOut comments or a call to the SNP backcountry office are the only way to know whether Calf Mountain, Blackrock, and Pinefield sources are flowing right now. Do not assume.
2. **Carry more capacity.** Even just upgrading to a 3L or 4L total carry (two 1.5L bottles plus a 1L dirty-water bag for your filter, for example) removes the single-point-of-failure problem. ## True Halfway vs. Mental Halfway

**True halfway (mile marker):** Pine Grove Furnace State Park, PA. This is the actual geographic midpoint of the Appalachian Trail — roughly AT mile 1,105.9 NOBO. The halfway marker is right there near the park. It's a simple roadside park with a general store, a small museum (the AT Museum), and a mix of day-use and overnight facilities. It feels like a quiet Pennsylvania state park, not a trail town.

**Mental halfway (emotional landmark):** Harpers Ferry, WV — home of the Appalachian Trail Conservancy headquarters. It lands around AT mile 1,024–1,025 NOBO, roughly 80 miles *before* the true halfway. For decades, Harpers Ferry was treated as the psychological midpoint because: the ATC lives there, it's a dramatic river-gap town with history and train tracks and ice cream, and hikers historically celebrated "halfway" there. It stuck. But it's not the real middle — you still have ~170 miles of northern Virginia, all of Maryland, and the start of Pennsylvania before you hit the actual halfway.

The practical difference: if you celebrate at Harpers Ferry, you still owe 80+ miles before the math actually splits the trail in half. Pine Grove Furnace is the real thing, but it's a quieter milestone — a state park, not a town.

## Harpers Ferry Weekend Overnight — Maryland Corridor (NOBO)

This is a **two-day, one-night plan** starting at Harpers Ferry / ATC HQ and heading north into Maryland. You get the mental halfway landmark right at the start, cross into Maryland within miles, and stay in the Mason-Dixon area without going anywhere near Pine Grove Furnace, Pennsylvania (that's ~65+ trail miles farther north — a different trip entirely).

### Day 1: Harpers Ferry / ATC HQ → Ed Garvey Memorial Shelter
**~18.9 miles**

- Start at ATC headquarters (AT mile ~1024.4). Touch the sign, grab a photo, then head north.
- Cross the Potomac River on the footbridge, enter Maryland through Weverton (~mile 1040.6) and Weverton Cliffs.
- Push to **Ed Garvey Memorial Shelter** (~mile 1043.3). This is a standard AT shelter in Maryland — verify current water source status and legal-use standing before you leave.
- This is a solid push for a weekend hiker. If 18.9 miles is too much on day one, the plan still works; I'll give you a shorter variant below.

### Day 2: Ed Garvey → Dahlgren Backpack Campground → Gathland State Park
**~11.7–17.7 miles**

- From Ed Garvey, head north to **Dahlgren Backpack Campground** (~mile 1055.0, ~11.7 mi). Dahlgren has restrooms, showers, and tent pads — good pickup point if you want an easier second day.
- If you want more miles, continue to **Gathland State Park / Crampton Gap** (~mile 1061.0, ~17.7 mi total day). Gathland has parking, road access, and historical context — easier shuttle pickup.

### Shorter Variant (if 19 miles day one is too big)

| Plan | Day 1 | Day 2 |
|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | ATC HQ → Ed Garvey (18.9) | Ed Garvey → Dahlgren (11.7) or Gathland (17.7) |
| **Moderate** | ATC HQ → Weverton area / dispersed legal (consult MD DNR) | → Ed Garvey or Dahlgren |

If you shift the first day shorter and stop near Weverton (~16.2 mi), you need to confirm legal overnight options there — Maryland has specific rules; Ed Garvey is the surer permitted overnight.

---

## What You Must Confirm Before Leaving

1. **Water at Ed Garvey Memorial Shelter** — seasonal; check FarOut recent comments or call Maryland DNR South Mountain before counting on it.
2. **Legal overnight at Dahlgren** — open status, any fee, reservation required? Confirm via Maryland DNR.
3. **Shuttle / parking** — where will you leave a car or get picked up? Harpers Ferry has limited overnight parking; Gathland or a local shuttle service may be your best exit.
4. **Virginia stomach bug** — the ATC alert is active right now through parts of VA. Wash hands, treat water, and be careful at shared facilities if your pre/post hike touches Virginia towns.

---

## What This Is NOT

- **Not Pine Grove Furnace.** That's Pennsylvania, AT mile ~1090+, another full multi-day push north. Different trip.
- **Not the Mason-Dixon line exactly.** The AT crosses it near Pen Mar, north of this corridor — but you're hiking through the Maryland borderlands the weekend is named for, which is the right feel.
